svg.aria-label: Channel depth is set by the permeability ceiling. Three schematic networks with ceilings x5.5, x10 and x20: the higher the ceiling, the more the open channel out-conducts filled paths and the larger its share of flow, so PR_V at the channel peak falls from about 0.78 to 0.67 to 0.61 of its start. Ceiling = 1/phi0 for gypsum only, 1 + (vf0/phi0)(1 - Gamma) when calcite replaces gypsum.
svg.text: ceiling = 1/φ₀ (gypsum only) · ceiling = 1 + (vf₀/φ₀)(1 − Γ) (coupled; vf₀ = 0.9, Γ = Vcal/Vgyp = 0.494)
a higher ceiling lets the open channel out-conduct its filled neighbours by more, so it draws a larger share of the flow: deeper channel
same ceiling → same depth (paired difference median about 0.01, max 0.03), whatever the chemistry; the channel stays on inherited paths (0.95–0.99) even at ×20
